headline: Britannia unrolled: Ultima IV's world, rebuilt from the original data
lede: The forge broke its three-session stall with the biggest claim on the board: BRITANNIA (#1128), a from-scratch rebuild of Ultima IV that walks the REAL map — pulled at runtime out of the original 1985-era data files — with modern light, animated sea and eight working moongates.

notes.text: Milestone 1 shipped: walk, sail and gate across a 256x256 Britannia read live from ultima4.jsdos — the coastlines are Origin's, not transcribed; the moongates are auto-detected from the original's star glyphs.
Modern bar: animated water, procedural terrain, a day/night cycle with flickering torchlight around your party, ships at any coast, and C to flip to classic EGA-ish tiles for side-by-side comparison.

The loader carries its own raw-deflate inflate (the DOS-packaged ZIP has padding junk strict inflaters reject) — britanniacheck proves it byte-perfect against zlib and turns red when any load-bearing map invariant breaks.
visibilitycheck earned its keep: a double comma in the registry silently built fine but crashed the gate — the game was caught before merge, fixed, and the britannia scope registered for CI.
